## 1. Identity & classification
- **ID:** 16027585017
- **Title:** [WCL][PO][UFS] BSOD after booting Windows through UFS as Primary Storage with PKGC states enabled
- **Program / release:** WCL (Wildcat Lake), `package.wclc-n204-a0`, stepping A0
- **Component:** `hw.storage` · **Owner:** msure · **Submitted:** 2025-05-29
- **Status:** workaround shipped (BIOS 14025261732 `complete`) — IP/RTL fix declined (16027667860 `wont_fix`); HSD field still reads `root_caused / awaiting_fix`
- **Signature tag:** `ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc` (power-state / link-PM class)
- **IP / layer:** UFS 3.1 host controller ↔ OCP (Sonics) fabric ↔ PMC; interaction with platform PKGC / S0ix power management
- **Scope:** one bug tracked across **4 HSD tickets in 3 teams** — this record consolidates them (see §10)

## 2. Symptom
- With UFS as primary storage + PKGC/S0ix enabled, Windows hits **BSOD, MCA, or hang/freeze** — after boot or after sleep exit (also seen as `DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION` and hard hang / CATERROR on the origin ticket).
- **Exact bugchecks** `[tf-minutes]`: **`DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION`** (WIP) and **`CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`** — the latter had a **memory dump captured and shared with MTC**.
- **Disappears when PKG C-states limited to C0/C1** — the single strongest clue that the trigger is deep-power-state entry, not the data path.
- **Tell-tale:** flood of UFS D0/D3 calls, then UFS non-responsive; PSF trace clean except the last transaction to the `IS_` register is stuck. (The D0/D3 flood shows as alternating `_PS3 UFS0` ↔ `_PS0 UFS0 D0` — evidence `Comment_3_second.png`.)
- **Depth reached at failure:** PKGC entry counters show C6_1=263 and C10_1=532, but C10_2/C10_3 = 0 (never entered); counts identical across two reads → counters frozen because the system was stuck (evidence `Comment_3.png`).
- **MCA is not guaranteed:** in one silicon capture `debug.mca.analyze()` came back empty even though the system had failed — so “no MCA” does not rule this out (evidence `Comment_3.png`).
- **Reproducibility profile:** deterministic under the failing config; gated by the Intel Gfx driver being installed (that's what lets the platform attempt PKGC). Uninstalling Gfx keeps the system in PKGC0 and masks the bug.

## 3. Initial triage
- **First signal:** system unstable booting Windows off UFS with S0ix; stable with PKGC off → immediately implicated power-state entry, not the raw data path.
- **Early discriminators tried:** ACPI dump (saw the abnormal D0/D3 flood); disabling PEP constraints for UFS → did not help; uninstalling the Gfx driver → masks it (stays in PKGC0).
- **Fastest confirm:** flip PKGC → C0/C1; if the system goes stable, you're on this class.
- **Rule-in (it IS this):** host-controller `IS_` shows **SBFES + HBFES** set (or last `IS_` read stuck in the PSF trace); MCA **THREE_STRIKE on CORE2 MLC** with a non-posted read stuck **PSF4 → UFS**; **PKGC-off → stable** holds.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this):** fails with PKGC fully disabled / no Gfx driver installed; no OCP fabric error (`SBFES`/`HBFES` clear) at the hang; failure on the raw data path rather than power-state entry/exit → look elsewhere.
- **Nearest look-alikes:** other UFS hangs that BSOD on boot but show a clean `IS_` and no PSF4→UFS stall (data-path/link-training issues) — the deciding tell is the **OCP fabric timeout + stuck non-posted read**, unique to this LTR-to-PMC class.

## 4. Reproduction recipe
- UFS = primary boot/storage on WCL; boot Windows with S0ix/PKGC enabled; Intel Gfx driver installed.
- ImageID `WCL-U-2024-CONS-25.21.3.222`; IFWI `WCL_UR01_A0A0-...01DE042A_UFS_2025WW22.3.01.bin` (regression IFWI `...015E042A_UFS_2025WW23.3.04.bin`); boot recipe `wcl_L0UP_204_GTen_32EU`.
- Origin-ticket bench: WCL DDR5 SODIMM T3 ERB, BKC/OS `10.0.26100`, UFS SK hynix `HN8T15DEHKX075`, HT disabled.
- **Expect:** BSOD/MCA/hang within ~10s of Windows boot, or on sleep exit.
- **Confirm it's THIS bug:** host-controller `IS_` has **SBFES + HBFES** set / last `IS_` read stuck in the PSF trace; or an MCA **THREE_STRIKE on CORE2 MLC** with a non-posted read stuck **PSF4 → UFS**.
- **Mitigation to avoid repro:** limit PKGC to C0/C1.

## 5. Logs / instrumentation — RANKED, with WHEN + HOW
Each entry: **WHEN** (the trigger/stage that tells you to grab it) → **HOW** (capture method) → **WHY** (what it yields). Collect decisive-first.
> **Full capture/decode procedure for every log below lives in the `unified-ufs-log-analysis` skill**
> (`how-to-capture-logs`). The HOW here is a summary; that skill is the source of truth.

**Decisive**
- **PSF trace** (fabric transaction trace)
  - **WHEN:** the moment you suspect the failure is power-state/fabric related (i.e., right after the "PKGC-off → stable" discriminator). **Arm it BEFORE triggering the failure** so it captures the failing signature at the hang — it is useless if armed after the hang.
  - **HOW:** arm trace on the failing signature, then run the boot/sleep-wake cycle that repros.
  - **WHY:** isolates the stuck `IS_` read / PSF4→UFS stall — the fingerprint.
- **Host-controller `IS_` register (SBFES + HBFES)**
  - **WHEN:** immediately **at the hang/BSOD**, before any reset/recovery runs (recovery can clobber it). If a watchdog reset is imminent, halt cores first.
  - **HOW:** ITP/PythonSV register read at the failure.
  - **WHY:** SBFES/HBFES set = OCP fabric-error confirmation.
- **MCA decode** (`debug.mca.analyze()` via PythonSV)
  - **WHEN:** right after an MCA/CATERROR/three-strike, **before power-cycling** (MCA banks are lost on reset).
  - **HOW:** PythonSV `debug.mca.analyze()`.
  - **WHY:** identifies THREE_STRIKE bank/core (e.g., CORE2 MLC). **Note:** may return **empty** (no MCA) for this signature — evidence `Comment_3.png` — so absence of MCA does not rule the class out.
- **VISA capture** (evidence: `Comment_10.png`)
  - **WHEN:** capture across the PKGC-exit window at the hang. Set up **before** the failing cycle.
  - **HOW:** VISA monitor-port signal capture; watch PMC/UFS power + ISM signals during the repro.
  - **WHY:** the decisive visual proof — shows **upstream cycle asserts `ufs_prim_clkreq` + `req_sa=1` for PkgC exit**, then **downstream `int_sts` read hangs**, with a measured **~804.432 µs** gap. Also proves UFS is still alive/accepting requests during the hang (rules out "device fell off the bus"). Key signals: `ufspw1_pmc_pgd0_pg_req_b`, `ufsx2_pmc_pgd0_pg_req_b`, `pmcm_cstate_ea`, `PMCMCPPMFA_ps`, `prim_ism_agent_in/fabric_in/fabric_out`.
- **PKGC entry counters** (`pm_tools.cstate.get_pkgc_entry_counters()` via PythonSV, evidence: `Comment_3.png`)
  - **WHEN:** at/around the hang, to see which package C-states were actually reached.
  - **HOW:** PythonSV `pm_tools.cstate.get_pkgc_entry_counters()`.
  - **WHY:** here **C10_1=532 reached, C10_2=C10_3=0** (reaches PKGC10.1, never deeper); identical across two reads = frozen at hang.

**Useful**
- **WinDbg stack (OS side)**
  - **WHEN:** at the BSOD/DPC_WATCHDOG, during live kernel debug (attach **before** the repro; full post-mortem dump was unreliable here).
  - **HOW:** live KD attach; `kv` / `.frame`.
  - **WHY:** shows `storufs!UfsResetBusDpc → UfsResetBus → UfsIntelLkfResetBus → UfsStopAdapter → storport!StorPortStallExecution` (reset >20s → watchdog).
- **ACPI dump**
  - **WHEN:** early, while characterizing OS behavior (before going to silicon) — captures the D0/D3 flood leading into the hang.
  - **HOW:** platform ACPI dump on the failing boot.
  - **WHY:** shows abnormal D0/D3 traffic (symptom, not cause).
- **PMC power-status regs** `ufsx2_pwr_sts`, `ufspw1_pwr_sts`
  - **WHEN:** at the hang, to check UFS power-gating state at failure.
  - **HOW:** PythonSV register read.
  - **WHY:** `=0x1` = not power-gated (UFS controller/clock still up).
- **PCIe Power Status Control register** (OS D0↔D3 flow check)
  - **WHEN:** when analyzing the OS D3-entry sequence.
  - **WHY:** OS-flow expectation noted in ticket — the link must be put into **Hibernate BEFORE** writing the PCIe Power Status Control register from **D0→D3**; a check item during D0/D3 flow analysis.
- **Solar app logs** (v3.25.204.0)
  - **WHEN:** during **fix validation** — across the full 100-cycle regression (S0ix/S4/S5/WR/CR), not during initial debug.
  - **HOW:** Solar app capture over the regression run.
  - **WHY:** pass/fail + S0ix residency (~85–88%) evidence.

**Noise / ruled-out**
- **PA (protocol analyzer)**
  - **WHEN:** only once electrical/SI is a live hypothesis — run it to *close* SI, not to open debug.
  - **WHY:** here it showed **no SI suspect** (door closed early).
- Registry tweaks (`LinkHibern8TimeoutInMS`, gear 4→2) → boundary experiments only; **did not fix**.

**Decisive-first capture sequence (bench recipe)**
1. Arm **VISA** + **PSF trace** on the failing signature. 2. Attach **WinDbg** live. 3. Trigger the repro (boot / sleep-wake). 4. At the hang, **halt cores immediately** and read **`IS_` (SBFES/HBFES)** + **PMC pwr_sts** + **MCA decode** *before* any reset/power-cycle. 5. Only then power-cycle. 6. Save VISA/PSF captures with the exact failing cycle ID.

## 6. Debug flow (timeline)
1. **Isolation:** PKGC off → stable; the Gfx-driver dependency was established (PKGC is only attempted with the Gfx driver installed).
2. **ACPI dump** → unexpected D0/D3 flood; disabling the PEP constraints didn't help.
3. **Large timeout-knob sweep** (`D3IdleTimeoutInMS`, `LinkHibern8TimeoutInMS`, `LinkHibern8ResidencyIntervalInUS`, `FeatureFlags`) across Software/Auto Hibernate — these are Windows OS **`storufs.inf`** driver settings; mapped which combinations were stable vs hang (see §6b).
4. **WW23.4 silicon look:** VISA showed UFS alive; PSF trace caught the `IS_` read stuck; PA cleared signal integrity.
5. **OS side (origin ticket):** WinDbg → storufs reset path, UFS bus reset >20s → DPC watchdog. **HW side:** MCA THREE_STRIKE on CORE2 MLC, non-posted read stuck PSF4→UFS.
6. **Hypothesis:** UFS issues an upstream posted write → wakes the system from PKGC → resources arrive too late → OCP fabric times out → FATAL error sets `IS_` → software's downstream `IS_` read never completes → hang.
7. **Root cause confirmed:** OCP fabric timeout waiting for a system resource; UFS 3.1 not requesting LTR to the PMC.
8. **Workaround** (650µs LTR, then selective ignore-LTR) engineered; the S0i2.1/2.2 side-effect was found and mitigated; 100-cycle regression passed.

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
- **OCP (Sonics) fabric timeout waiting for a system resource** during PKGC. **WCL UFS 3.1 does not request an LTR to the PMC.** When UFS issues an upstream posted write to memory (waking the system from a deep C-state) and then needs core/ring/memory resources, they arrive too late; the fabric times out and sets host-controller `IS_` bits **SBFES/HBFES**. Software's downstream read of `IS_` never completes → stuck transaction → BSOD/MCA/hang. On the OS side, the recovery **UFS bus reset takes >20s**, tripping the **DPC watchdog**.
- **PMC side of the resource gap** `[tf-minutes, WW23.3]`: **PMC ignores the D3 requirement for UFS**, and **PMC requires the subsystem power to be down for S0ix entry**. So when UFS wakes upstream mid-PKGC, PMC has not kept the resource available → exactly the late-resource condition that trips the OCP timeout.
- **Signal-level confirmation** `[confirmed via VISA capture, evidence: Comment_10.png]`: the **upstream cycle from UFS asserts `ufs_prim_clkreq` and drives `req_sa=1` to force a PkgC exit**; the driver's **downstream read of `int_sts` then hangs**. The measured interval between the upstream wake request and the hung downstream read is **~804.432 µs**. Related PMC/UFS signals in the capture: `ufspw1_pmc_pgd0_pg_req_b`, `ufsx2_pmc_pgd0_pg_req_b`, `pmcm_cstate_ea`, `PMCMCPPMFA_ps` (0x0→0x4→0x0), `prim_ism_agent_in/fabric_in/fabric_out`.
- **Class:** design/architecture (missing LTR reporting), surfaced by platform power-management interaction. **Latent since LKF era**, with differing behavior across LKF/ADL/WCL.
- **Refined statement** `[tf-minutes, WW24.1]`: root cause = **"OCP Timeout waiting for the system resource"**; workaround = write/report **650µs** as UFS LTR.
- **Detailed fabric hypothesis** `[tf-minutes]`: UFS receives an OS/SW transaction and issues an **upstream posted** transaction to memory → that upstream cycle **wakes the system from PKGC**. Because it is posted there is **no completion message in the trace** (unknown if it reached memory). The **UFS OCP fabric times out** after the upstream transaction → **FATAL error in `IS_`**. The OS then reads `IS_` to check completion, but the already-hung fabric **never answers the downstream read** → hang.
- **Why it hits Windows but not Chrome** `[confirmed — HSD ticket + tf-minutes]`: the root cause (OCP fabric timeout from the missing LTR + PMC not honoring UFS D3) is **OS-agnostic** — it is **not** RTD3-specific and Auto-H8 (AH8) is not "broken." What differs is the **OS power-flow cadence** that decides *when* UFS wakes upstream relative to PKGC residency:
  - **ChromeOS** uses **Auto-H8 only**. It reaches PC10/S0i2.x (LP5 Rev2; Rev1 stopped hanging after a **PECI-noise rework**). Its timing never opens the failing window.
  - **Windows** storufs does **SW hibernate then `_PS3()`** and, per §6b, **Auto-Hibernate configs mostly hang** while tuned **Software-Hibernate configs are stable** — i.e., the Windows D3/hibernate-vs-PKGC-residency *timing* is what lets UFS issue an upstream wake before PMC has restored the resource.
  - **RTD3 is NOT the differentiator** — the issue **reproduced on a non-RTD3 Windows image** (Roopa, WW23.4; also in the HSD ticket), and the minutes note **no signature pins the failure on RTD3 + AH8 together**. The team's early "RTD3 implicated" framing was a hypothesis that this repro disproved.
- **Confirming silicon observations** `[tf-minutes]`: during the failure UFS is **active and accepting requests** (VISA monitor-port); PA capture showed **no signal-integrity suspect**; disabling **PMC Force Alignment** alone reached PKGC10.3; the issue also **reproduced on a non-RTD3 Windows image**.

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`IS_` bits `SBFES` (bit 17) + `HCFES` (bit 16)** are the confirmation: both are **fatal, non-recoverable** UFSHCI error-status bits. When set, the host-controller core **stops** and the OS's `IS_` read hangs → BSOD/MCA and the >20s reset. SBFES = the system-bus/**OCP-fabric timeout**; HCFES = host-controller fatal.
- **Naming:** the sighting writes **"HBFES"**, but the register spec + MindShare training define IS bit 16 as **`HCFES`** — no "HBFES" exists in either doc. Read HBFES ≡ HCFES.
- Full bit-level decode (offsets, access, enable bits, spec-verbatim text) → **`reference/ufs-glossary.md` → "`IS_` Interrupt Status — detailed decode."**

## 8. Fix & verification (workaround + status)
- **No IP/RTL fix** — the IP/PCH ticket (16027667860) was **rejected / wont_fix**; fix pushed to BIOS.
- **Workaround:** report **UFS LTR ≈ 650µs** → stable (PKGC10.3, S0i2.0). **Why it works:** the LTR tells the PMC "service UFS within 650µs," so the PMC won't enter any state whose resource-restore latency exceeds that — guaranteeing core/ring/memory come back fast enough that a UFS upstream wake mid-PKGC can't outrun them → no fabric timeout. **Why it's too blunt:** asserted permanently, the 650µs bound also **blocks S0i2.1/S0i2.2** (their exit latencies exceed 650µs), costing the deepest S0ix residency.
- **Refined BIOS mitigation:** ignore/disqualify UFS LTR on UFS-D3 / S0ix entry; re-qualify on D0 / S0ix exit. Test BIOS `..._AUTO_LTR_0x8A8A_PS0_PS3_ignufsx2_debug_fix.rom`. **Why done this way:** during **D3 / S0ix entry the IP is idle** and will not issue an upstream transaction, so it does **not** need the latency guarantee then — dropping the LTR lets the platform reach S0i2.1/2.2 (residency regained, safely). Re-qualifying on **D0 / S0ix exit** restores the 650µs guard the instant UFS can be active again. Net: stability while active **and** deep residency while idle.
- **Verification:** **100 cycles pass** (UFS primary) across S0ix/S4/S5/WR/CR; S0ix residency ~85–88% (Solar logs). Landed/closed via BIOS ticket 14025261732 (`complete` / `workaround`).
- **Follow-ups:** review 650µs LTR in WCL PCD Design CCB; file BIOS RCR.

### 8b. Authoritative fix-experiment matrix (TF minutes, WW23.5→WW24.1) `[tf-minutes]`
Each experiment = hypothesis → configuration → pass/fail. This is what explains **why the fix is the fix**.
| # | Configuration | Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---------------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Vary `D3IdleTimeoutInMS` / `LinkHibernateTimeoutInMS` (storufs.inf) | OS-timeout interplay | Inconclusive — OCP timeout still seen |
| 2 | OCP-timeout-disable WA + SW Hibernate | WA only applies on `_PS0()/_PS3()`; AH8 not aligned to OS D3 | **Fail** — timeout persists (resources gone once PKGC entered) |
| 3 | OCP-timeout-disable WA + SW-H8 + Auto LTR 650µs | OS skips PS3/PS0 during PKGC, so LTR is needed | **Pass** |
| 4 | SW-H8 + Auto LTR 650µs | LTR ensures resource availability | **Pass** (room for better IP power-gating) |
| 5 | AH8 + Auto LTR 650µs | Best IP PG efficiency during PKGC | **Pass** — caveat: Auto-LTR **may be reset during SoC PM flows** |
| 6 | AH8 + Auto LTR 650µs + **BIOS qualify/disqualify LTR on S0ix exit/entry** | Don't apply LTR while IP is idle in S0ix | **WIP** — the final refined mitigation |
- **Prior-art WA reused:** an existing **"ADL OCP Timeout Work Around"** was ported into **WCL Coreboot FW** (Archana). `[tf-minutes]`

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Avoidable:** LTR-to-PMC reporting is a known-class gap since LKF. A cross-program checklist ("does the IP report LTR before PKGC is enabled with it as boot device?") would likely have caught it pre-silicon.
- **Prevention:** add LTR-reporting validation + OCP-fabric-timeout monitoring (`SBFES`/`HBFES`) to the UFS+S0ix bring-up suite; default-on capture of `IS_`/MCA on hang.
- **Detection gap:** only manifests with Gfx driver installed (PKGC attempted) — easy to miss if power-management config isn't in the default matrix.
- **Dead-ends / false leads:**
  - Disabling **PEP constraints** for UFS — did **not** help; ruled out software power-policy as the cause.
  - Uninstalling the **Gfx driver** — masks the failure (stays in PKGC0) but is not a fix; misled early triage toward graphics rather than the UFS LTR-to-PMC gap.
  - Treating it as a raw data-path / link-training failure — the clean data path but stuck **PSF4→UFS non-posted read** ruled this out; the fault is fabric power-state, not the UFS link.

## 12. Debug story (conversational narrative for first-time readers)

**Where it starts — the smell of the problem.** You're bringing up WCL with UFS as the primary
storage device — Windows boots from UFS. Everything's fine until you enable deep power
management (Package C-states / S0ix). Then: sometimes a BSOD, sometimes an MCA, sometimes just a
hang — right after boot, or after waking from sleep. The most valuable free clue: **turn PKGC off
(C0/C1) and it's rock solid.** That reframes everything — this is not data corruption or a UFS
read-path bug; it's about *entering a deep power state while UFS is the boot device.* That's your
north star.

**First real look — what is the OS doing?** You grab an ACPI dump during the failure and see
Windows firing a **flood of D0/D3 power transitions** at UFS, far more than the config warrants;
the IP eventually stops responding. You try the obvious lever — **disable PEP constraints** for
UFS — and it *still* hangs. Important negative result: the D0/D3 flood is a symptom, not the
cause. Don't anchor on it.

**The long, unglamorous sweep.** Maybe the timeout knobs are wrong. You methodically sweep
`D3IdleTimeoutInMS`, `LinkHibern8TimeoutInMS`, `LinkHibern8ResidencyIntervalInUS`, `FeatureFlags`
across Software- and Auto-Hibernate, tabulating {PKGC reached, S0ix yes/no, hang yes/no}. Some
combos are stable, some hang. This gives you **boundary data**, not the why — and that's fine.

**The clarifying accident.** Someone asks: can you repro with the Intel Gfx driver *uninstalled*?
You try — and it **won't fail** without it. Why? The platform only *attempts* PKGC when the Gfx
driver lets the system idle deep. Uninstall it → stays PKGC0 → bug can't fire. Not a fix — a
**confirmation of the trigger condition**, and it nails your minimum repro.

**Going below the OS.** Now you watch the silicon at the moment of death. Three captures, in
order: **VISA** (monitor-port) shows UFS is **still alive and accepting requests** — it didn't die,
it's stuck mid-transaction. **PSF trace** shows everything normal *except* the **last `IS_`
(Interrupt Status) register read is stuck** — it goes out and never completes. That stuck read is
the fingerprint. **PA capture** checks signal integrity → clean, no SI suspect (a good door to
close early).

**On the OS side (the origin ticket), the crash tells the same story from above.** WinDbg shows a
DPC watchdog assertion with a long-running DPC in the storufs reset path — `UfsResetBusDpc →
UfsResetBus → UfsIntelLkfResetBus → UfsStopAdapter → StorPortStallExecution` — i.e., the **UFS bus
reset is taking 20+ seconds** and tripping the watchdog. And HW analysis finds an **MCA
THREE_STRIKE on CORE2's MLC bank**, tied to a **downstream non-posted read to UFS getting stuck
between PSF4 and UFS.** Two faces, one failure.

**The "aha".** UFS receives an OS request, needs data from memory, and issues an **upstream posted
write** toward memory. That cycle **wakes the system out of PKGC**. Because it's *posted*, there's
**no completion in the trace** — you can't even tell if it reached memory. The resources it needs
aren't ready yet (system was deep asleep), so the **fabric times out**, raising a FATAL error and
setting `IS_` bits **SBFES/HBFES**. The OS then does a **downstream read of `IS_`** to service the
request — but the fabric is already hung, so that read never returns. That's your stuck
transaction, your MCA, your BSOD. Confirmed root cause: **OCP fabric timeout waiting for a system
resource**, because **WCL UFS 3.1 never requests an LTR to the PMC.** And this class has existed
**since LKF**, showing up differently on LKF/ADL/WCL — exactly the "we've seen this shape before"
that this database exists to flag.

**The fix — and why the first one wasn't enough.** The clean fix would be in RTL (make UFS report
LTR); not available here (IP ticket rejected → BIOS). So: **report UFS LTR ≈ 650µs** — tells the
PMC not to go so deep that UFS starves. Stable, reaches PKGC10.3 / S0i2.0. *But* 650µs is blunt —
it **blocks the deeper S0i2.1/S0i2.2**, hurting power. Refined fix: be smart about *when* the LTR
applies — **ignore it during UFS-D3 / S0ix entry, re-qualify on D0 / S0ix exit.** Now you get both
stability and deep S0ix. Proof: **100-cycle regression** across S0ix/S4/S5/WR/CR all pass, ~85–88%
S0ix residency (Solar logs).

**If you're reproducing this tomorrow — the short recipe.** WCL, UFS primary, boot Windows (Gfx
driver installed), enable S0ix/PKGC, do boot + sleep-wake cycles → expect BSOD/MCA/hang. Confirm
it's *this* bug via PSF trace + `IS_` **SBFES/HBFES** set (or MCA THREE_STRIKE with PSF4→UFS
stuck). Sanity control: limit PKGC to C0/C1 → stable.

**Honest caveats.** The exact BSOD bugcheck/minidump was never decoded; the full MCA status wasn't
preserved; the decisive traces are referenced but not retrievable through tooling; and whether the
650µs + selective-ignore-LTR BIOS workaround is the *permanent* answer (vs an IP LTR fix in a
later stepping) is left open. Ask msure/roopaheg for the attachments and the BIOS RCR.
